title: Collection of Environmental Samples for Screening Influenza A Viruses
author: Bhumika Prajapati

steps.title: Prepare Personal Protective Equipment
steps.instruction: Equip hands with sterile rubber gloves and wear a fresh N95 mask. Sterilize gloves with 70-80% ethanol before initiating sample collection.

steps.title: Collect Water Samples
steps.instruction: Collect water samples from wetland waterbody surfaces or poultry water at locations with high bird activity.

substeps.instruction: Collect a minimum of 500 mL of water in a sterile 1 L jerry can.
Sterilize gloves with 70-80% ethanol post-collection.
Label the container with waterproof permanent markers including sample type, location/site name, and date of collection.
Store samples in a potable refrigerator at 4ºC.

steps.title: Collect Fecal Samples
steps.instruction: Collect fresh fecal material from locations with high bird activity.

substeps.instruction: Collect approximately 2-3 g of fecal matter into 3 mL of VTM using sterile autoclaved wooden spoons (quantity may be augmented relative to vial volume).
Label the container with waterproof permanent markers including sample type, location/site name, and date of collection.
Immediately store VTMs in an ice box maintained at 4ºC.

steps.title: Collect Feather Samples
steps.instruction: Collect molted feathers from wetlands or poultry fowls at locations with high bird activity.

substeps.instruction: Collect 3 to 5 feathers from a single sampling site (preferably different species) and store in 3 mL VTM, ensuring the quill or calamus is dipped in the VTM.
Label the container with waterproof permanent markers including sample type, location/site name, and date of collection.
Immediately store VTMs in an ice box maintained at 4ºC.

steps.title: Collect Sediment Soil Samples
steps.instruction: Collect sediment soil samples from the banks of wetland water bodies at locations with high bird activity.

substeps.instruction: Collect samples in sterile 50 mL centrifuge tubes, sampling from different locations at the same site to maximize area coverage.
Label the container with waterproof permanent markers including sample type, location/site name, and date of collection.
Store samples at 4ºC.

steps.title: Collect Air Samples
steps.instruction: Use an air sampler to collect environmental air samples.

substeps.instruction: Place the air sampler at a minimum height of 1 meter above ground level (using a tripod or manually) and within 1–2 meters of the collection site.
Using sterile forceps and gloves, install a sterile gelatin filter (pore size: 3 microns, diameter: 80 mm) using the provided fitting apparatus, ensuring the filter does not break.
Switch on the air sampler for 20 minutes with preset parameters (50 L/minutes) to collect a total volume of 1000 L.
Remove the gelatin filter with clean forceps and collect it in 6 mL of VTM; gently shake to dissolve the filter.
Label the container with waterproof permanent markers including sample type, location/site name, and date of collection.
Store the VTM vial at 4ºC.
Sterilize the air sampler with 70-80% ethanol before moving to a new sampling location.

steps.title: Collect Surface Swabs
steps.instruction: Collect surface swabs from poultry farms using electrostatic dust cloth (EDC) pieces.

substeps.instruction: Use sterile EDC cloth pieces to swab surfaces, covering the maximum area of the poultry environment.
Use different EDC swabs for different locations or different cages.
Submerge the collected swab in sterile 50 mL centrifuge tubes.
Label the container with waterproof permanent markers including sample type, location/site name, and date of collection.
Store swabs at 4ºC.
Collect approximately 2-3 g of poultry litter in 3 mL of VTM.
Label the container with waterproof permanent markers including sample type, location/site name, and date of collection.
Immediately store VTMs in an ice box maintained at 4ºC.

steps.title: Post-Collection Disposal and Reset
steps.instruction: Properly dispose of contaminated materials and reset PPE for new sites.

substeps.instruction: Discard used gloves, masks, and wooden spoons in biohazard bags immediately after each collection process.
Use a fresh pair of sterile gloves and a mask for subsequent sample collection sites.
